name: Shev Bhaji
steps: Dry-roast coconut and half the onion over low heat for 5–6 minutes until brown and nutty. Cool and grind with garlic and ginger to a thick paste.
Heat oil in a pan. Cook remaining onion for 6 minutes until golden. Stir in the coconut paste and roast 4 minutes, scraping the bottom.
Add tomato, kala masala, chili powder and salt; cook 5 minutes until the masala darkens and oil shows at the edges.
Pour in 450 ml water and simmer uncovered 8 minutes to make a spicy, pourable rassa. Taste the salt before adding shev.
Add half the thick shev just before serving, ladle curry into bowls and top with remaining shev and coriander. Serve with jowar bhakri while some shev stays crisp.
tips: This Maharashtrian onion-coconut rassa is distinct from Gujarati tomato-based sev sabzi.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
